From her lonely lighthouse, Lyra flashed Morse code across the dark waves every night: *Are you there?*

Two hundred feet below, Jax, a deep-sea welder repairing trench cables, saw the light pulsing through the abyss. He flicked his torch back: *Always.*

They’d never met, bound only by signals.

Tonight, Jax’s suit alarm shrieked—oxygen failing. His light flickered out. 

Above, the ocean went pitch black. Lyra gasped.

Come back for the next part tomorrow.
